title: Resilient reset protocol for overlapping epoch quota windows
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Some tenants with a mix of hosted and reserved capacity have experienced transient double-charging or temporary under-allocation during rollovers when multiple quota epochs overlap (daily rolling windows + monthly anchored windows + reserved pool lease renewals). Edge cases include clock skew across region controllers, delayed lease checkpointing, and consumer retries that get replayed after a reset.

Goal: Design and implement a resilient reset protocol and reconciliation path that ensures a single authoritative quota reset per tenant per logical epoch, eliminates duplicate consumption during overlap windows, and provides clear backfill/recovery for orphaned usage. The solution must work for rolling windows (N-minute/hour/day), anchored monthly resets, and reserved-capacity lease intervals, and be compatible with current billing pipeline and billing-export formats.
acceptance_criteria: Single authoritative reset is observable in audit logs for each tenant epoch with at most one effective reset timestamp per epoch
No customers are charged twice for the same tokens in repeat/retry scenarios after an epoch boundary under normal network partitions
Backfill job can detect and reconcile orphaned consumptions within a configurable lookback (default 72h) and emit corrective billing adjustments to billing pipeline
Migration path for reserved pools: graceful cutover without service interruption and unit tests covering lease renewal overlap cases
Performance: reset path adds <5ms median overhead to hot-path token accounting under steady state
implementation_plan: Design: introduce a ResetCoordinator service per-tenant that elects (via lease) a single reset marker for each logical epoch; markers include epoch id, source (rolling|anchored|reserved), and monotonic sequence
Accounting changes: make token-commit idempotent by attaching epoch marker and commit-id; token writes that reference an already-committed commit-id are no-ops
Lease changes: extend reserved-pool lease checkpoint to include 'pending-reset' flag to avoid simultaneous resets during near-term renewals
Backfill: implement a reconcile job that scans token-commit logs for unknown epoch markers and either credits or tags them for manual review depending on magnitude
Observability: add reset-markers as traces and create dashboards showing reset-rate, collision-rate, and reconciled adjustments
Rollout: run in canary with 10 tenants in eu-west then 100 tenants across regions, enable feature-flagged fallback to legacy reset if problems detected
rollback_plan: Feature-flagged gate: disable ResetCoordinator at service-level; schedule recompute of recent epoch markers and revert commits made under new commit-id semantics via backfill pipeline. If cascade detected, revert to legacy reset algorithm and open high-severity incident to restore user quotas.
observability_changes: Trace spans for ResetCoordinator.elect and ResetCoordinator.markApplied
Audit log entry per authoritative reset: /logs/quota_resets with fields (tenant, epoch_id, marker_id, source, applied_at, coordinator_id)
Billing export tag: applied_reset_marker included on daily exports for downstream billing consumer
notes_and_decisions: Reviewed two designs: (A) centralized ResetCoordinator per-region; (B) fully decentralized marker election using vector clocks. Chose (A) because it has simpler failure semantics and easier auditability for billing compliance.

Trade-off: centralized coordinator increases small availability blast radius in a region. Mitigation: multi-zone replicas with fast failover and fallback to legacy idempotent-commit path for <1% of requests.
We will not attempt to change downstream billing export format in this sprint beyond adding applied_reset_marker; larger billing schema migration deferred to billing-2026.2
comments: 2026-03-02 - Rohit Kumar: Initial spike completed. Prototype of ResetCoordinator can elect a marker in 12ms median under load. Identified race when two coordinators run in different AZs due to delayed lease expiry.
2026-03-04 - Emily Zhang (PM): Please capture compliance requirements: audits must show authoritative marker for 24 months. Add retention to audit log plan.
2026-03-06 - Design review: DES-114 suggested adding a human-review queue for adjustments > $500 to reduce billing noise. Agreed to add threshold config.

2026-03-08 - Security: security review requested; threat model updated to include attacker forging epoch markers. Mitigation: sign markers with region KMS key. (see PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/982)
2026-03-09 - Implementation update: idempotent commit syscall added to accounting layer; integration tests added for replay, clock-skew, and consumer retry scenarios. Perf regression <2% p90 latency.
2026-03-10 - QA: Started canary with tenant cohort in eu-west; observed two small adjustments from reconcile job (total $12.34 across cohort). No double-charges reported by customers.
